entries.meaning: toward the head or upper part of a structure; above
examples: The nose is superior to the mouth.

entries.meaning: away from the head; toward the lower part of a structure; below
examples: The stomach is inferior to the diaphragm.

entries.meaning: toward the front of the body
examples: The sternum is anterior to the heart.

entries.meaning: toward the back of the body
examples: The spinal cord is posterior to the esophagus.

entries.meaning: toward the front (belly side) of the body; in humans, the same as anterior
examples: The chest and abdomen are on the ventral side of the body.

entries.meaning: toward the back of the body; in humans, the same as posterior
examples: The vertebral column is on the dorsal side of the body.

entries.meaning: toward the midline of the body
examples: The nose is medial to the eyes.

entries.meaning: away from the midline of the body; toward the side
examples: The ears are lateral to the eyes.

entries.meaning: between a more medial and a more lateral structure
examples: The intermediate cuneiform lies between the medial and lateral cuneiforms.

entries.meaning: the imaginary vertical line that divides the body into equal right and left halves
examples: The sternum lies on the midline of the chest.

entries.meaning: closer to the point where a limb attaches to the trunk, or to the origin of a structure
examples: The elbow is proximal to the wrist.

entries.meaning: farther from the point where a limb attaches to the trunk, or from the origin of a structure
examples: The fingers are distal to the wrist.

entries.meaning: toward or at the body surface; also called external
examples: The skin is superficial to the skeletal muscles.

entries.meaning: away from the body surface; more internal
examples: The bones of the arm are deep to its muscles.

entries.meaning: at or toward the center of the body or of a structure
examples: The brain and spinal cord form the central nervous system.

entries.meaning: extending outward from a central point; toward the outer part of a structure
examples: Peripheral nerves branch out from the spinal cord to the limbs.

entries.meaning: on both sides of the body; describes paired structures
examples: The kidneys are bilateral organs, one on each side.

entries.meaning: on only one side of the body
examples: The spleen is a unilateral organ on the left side.

entries.meaning: on the same side of the body
examples: The right arm and right leg are ipsilateral.

entries.meaning: on the opposite side of the body
examples: The right arm and left leg are contralateral.

entries.meaning: toward the head, similar to superior; also, relating to the skull (cranial region)
examples: The thorax is cranial to the abdomen.

entries.meaning: toward the tail or lower end of the body, similar to inferior
examples: The sacrum is caudal to the lumbar vertebrae.

entries.meaning: toward the nose or front of the head; used mainly to describe the brain
examples: The frontal lobe is rostral to the occipital lobe.

entries.meaning: a vertical plane that divides the body into right and left parts
examples: A sagittal plane runs from front to back and separates right from left.

entries.meaning: a sagittal plane through the midline that divides the body into equal right and left halves; also called the median plane
examples: A midsagittal section through the head cuts the nose into equal halves.

entries.meaning: a sagittal plane off the midline that divides the body into unequal right and left parts
examples: A parasagittal section through the head passes through one eye.

entries.meaning: a vertical plane that divides the body into anterior and posterior parts; also called the coronal plane
examples: A frontal plane separates the face from the back of the head.

entries.meaning: a plane that divides the body into superior and inferior parts; also called the horizontal plane
examples: A transverse plane through the waist separates the upper body from the lower body.

entries.meaning: a cut perpendicular to the long axis of a body part or organ; a transverse section of the body
examples: A cross section of a blood vessel shows a ring of wall around the open center.

entries.meaning: a cut along the long axis of a body part or organ
examples: A longitudinal section of a long bone shows the medullary cavity along the shaft.

entries.meaning: a cut made at an angle, between a cross section and a longitudinal section
examples: An oblique section of a tube produces an oval cut surface.

entries.meaning: the flat cut surface produced when the body or an organ is cut along a plane
examples: CT and MRI images show the body as a series of sections.

entries.meaning: the head, neck, and trunk; the central axis of the body
examples: The axial region includes the head, neck, and trunk.

entries.meaning: the upper and lower limbs, which attach to the axial region
examples: The arms and legs make up the appendicular region.

entries.meaning: the head
examples: The cephalic region includes the face and skull.

entries.meaning: the forehead
examples: The frontal region lies above the eyes.

entries.meaning: the eye area, around the bony eye socket
examples: The eyeball sits in the orbital region.

entries.meaning: the ear
examples: Otic drops are placed in the ear.

entries.meaning: the nose
examples: The nasal region is medial to the orbital regions.

entries.meaning: the mouth
examples: The oral region is inferior to the nasal region.

entries.meaning: the cheek
examples: The buccal region lies lateral to the oral region.

entries.meaning: the chin
examples: The mental region is the most inferior part of the face.

entries.meaning: the lower back of the head
examples: The occipital region is posterior to the ears.

entries.meaning: the neck
examples: The cervical region connects the head to the trunk.

entries.meaning: the point of the shoulder
examples: The acromial region is the top of the shoulder.

entries.meaning: the chest
examples: The thoracic region contains the heart and lungs.

entries.meaning: the middle of the chest, over the sternum
examples: The sternal region lies on the anterior midline of the chest.

entries.meaning: the chest, especially the upper chest
examples: The pectoral region lies over the large chest muscles.

entries.meaning: the breast
examples: The mammary regions are lateral to the sternal region.

entries.meaning: the ribs
examples: The costal region lies over the ribs on each side of the chest.

entries.meaning: the armpit
examples: Lymph nodes in the axillary region drain the upper limb.

entries.meaning: the abdomen, between the chest and the pelvis
examples: The abdominal region lies inferior to the thoracic region.

entries.meaning: the abdomen; same as abdominal
examples: The celiac region is another name for the abdominal region.

entries.meaning: the navel (umbilicus); also the central region of the nine abdominopelvic regions
examples: The umbilical region is the center square of the nine-region grid.

entries.meaning: the groin, where the thigh meets the trunk; also another name for the iliac abdominopelvic regions
examples: An inguinal hernia forms in the groin.

entries.meaning: the area over the pubic bones, just above the external genitalia; also another name for the hypogastric region
examples: The pubic region is inferior to the umbilical region.

entries.meaning: the pelvis, the lower part of the trunk between the hips
examples: The pelvic region contains the urinary bladder.

entries.meaning: the hip
examples: The coxal region is on the side of the body where the thigh joins the trunk.

entries.meaning: the region between the anus and the external genitalia
examples: The perineal region forms the floor of the trunk.

entries.meaning: the external reproductive organs
examples: The genital region is inferior to the pubic region.

entries.meaning: the back; also the upper surface of the hand or foot
examples: Dorsiflexion moves the toes toward the dorsum of the foot.

entries.meaning: the shoulder blade
examples: The scapular regions lie on the upper back.

entries.meaning: the spinal column, along the midline of the back
examples: The vertebral region runs down the middle of the back.

entries.meaning: the lower back between the ribs and the hips; also the right and left middle regions of the nine abdominopelvic regions
examples: Lower back pain is felt in the lumbar region.

entries.meaning: the area between the hips at the base of the spine, over the sacrum
examples: The sacral region is inferior to the lumbar region.

entries.meaning: the buttocks
examples: Intramuscular injections are often given in the gluteal region.

entries.meaning: the arm, from shoulder to elbow
examples: The biceps brachii lies in the brachial region.

entries.meaning: the front of the elbow
examples: Blood is usually drawn from a vein in the antecubital region.

entries.meaning: the elbow
examples: The median cubital vein crosses the front of the elbow.

entries.meaning: the back of the elbow
examples: The olecranal region is the point of the elbow.

entries.meaning: the forearm, from elbow to wrist
examples: The antebrachial region is distal to the brachial region.

entries.meaning: the wrist
examples: The carpal region contains eight small bones.

entries.meaning: the palm of the hand
examples: In anatomical position the palmar surfaces face forward.

entries.meaning: the fingers or toes
examples: Each digital region contains small bones called phalanges.

entries.meaning: the thumb
examples: In anatomical position the pollex is the most lateral finger.

entries.meaning: the thigh
examples: The femur is the bone of the femoral region.

entries.meaning: the front of the knee
examples: The kneecap lies in the patellar region.

entries.meaning: the back of the knee
examples: The popliteal pulse is felt behind the knee.

entries.meaning: the leg, from knee to ankle, especially its front
examples: The shin lies in the crural region.

entries.meaning: the calf, the back of the leg
examples: The calf muscles form the sural region.

entries.meaning: the lateral side of the leg; also called peroneal
examples: The fibular region lies on the outer side of the leg.

entries.meaning: the ankle
examples: The tarsal region connects the leg to the foot.

entries.meaning: the foot
examples: Pedal pulses are checked on the foot.

entries.meaning: the heel
examples: The calcaneal region is the posterior part of the foot.

entries.meaning: the sole of the foot
examples: The plantar surface touches the ground when you stand.

entries.meaning: the great toe
examples: The hallux is the most medial toe.

entries.meaning: the upper right quarter of the abdominopelvic area, marked off by two lines crossing at the umbilicus
examples: Most of the liver and the gallbladder are in the right upper quadrant.

entries.meaning: the upper left quarter of the abdominopelvic area, marked off by two lines crossing at the umbilicus
examples: Most of the stomach and the spleen are in the left upper quadrant.

entries.meaning: the lower right quarter of the abdominopelvic area, marked off by two lines crossing at the umbilicus
examples: The appendix is usually in the right lower quadrant.

entries.meaning: the lower left quarter of the abdominopelvic area, marked off by two lines crossing at the umbilicus
examples: The sigmoid colon lies in the left lower quadrant.

entries.meaning: the right and left upper regions of the nine abdominopelvic regions, just below the rib cartilages
examples: Most of the liver lies in the right hypochondriac region.

entries.meaning: the upper middle region of the nine abdominopelvic regions, over the stomach
examples: Heartburn is often felt in the epigastric region.

entries.meaning: the right and left lower regions of the nine abdominopelvic regions, near the hip bones; also called inguinal
examples: The appendix is usually in the right iliac region.

entries.meaning: the lower middle region of the nine abdominopelvic regions, below the umbilical region; also called pubic
examples: A full urinary bladder rises into the hypogastric region.

entries.meaning: the cavity made of the cranial cavity and vertebral canal; OpenStax calls it the posterior cavity
examples: The dorsal cavity holds the brain and spinal cord.

entries.meaning: the space inside the skull that houses the brain
examples: The cranial cavity is part of the dorsal cavity.

entries.meaning: the space inside the vertebral column that houses the spinal cord; also called the spinal cavity
examples: The spinal cord runs through the vertebral canal.

entries.meaning: the large cavity in the front of the trunk, made of the thoracic and abdominopelvic cavities; OpenStax calls it the anterior cavity
examples: The diaphragm divides the ventral cavity into upper and lower parts.

entries.meaning: the part of the ventral cavity above the diaphragm, inside the chest wall
examples: The heart and lungs are in the thoracic cavity.

entries.meaning: the thin fluid-filled space between the parietal and visceral pleura around each lung
examples: Each lung lies within its own pleural cavity.

entries.meaning: the central region of the thoracic cavity between the lungs, containing the heart, esophagus, trachea, thymus, and large blood vessels
examples: The heart sits in the mediastinum.

entries.meaning: the thin fluid-filled space between the parietal and visceral pericardium around the heart
examples: Fluid in the pericardial cavity lets the heart beat with little friction.

entries.meaning: the part of the ventral cavity below the diaphragm, made of the abdominal and pelvic cavities
examples: The abdominopelvic cavity holds most of the digestive organs.

entries.meaning: the upper part of the abdominopelvic cavity, holding the stomach, liver, spleen, gallbladder, and most of the intestines
examples: The liver is in the abdominal cavity.

entries.meaning: the lower part of the abdominopelvic cavity, surrounded by the pelvic bones
examples: The urinary bladder is in the pelvic cavity.

entries.meaning: the mouth cavity, containing the teeth and tongue
examples: Digestion begins in the oral cavity.

entries.meaning: the space inside the nose, behind the nostrils
examples: Air is warmed and moistened in the nasal cavity.

entries.meaning: the bony socket that holds an eye; also called the orbit
examples: Each eye sits in an orbital cavity.

entries.meaning: the small air-filled space in the temporal bone that holds the tiny ear bones
examples: The middle ear cavity contains three small bones that carry sound.

entries.meaning: a thin double-layered membrane that lines the ventral cavity walls and covers its organs, and secretes serous fluid
examples: The pleura is the serous membrane of the lungs.

entries.meaning: the thin watery fluid between the layers of a serous membrane that reduces friction
examples: Serous fluid lets the lungs slide smoothly during breathing.

entries.meaning: relating to the wall of a cavity; the layer of a serous membrane that lines the cavity wall
examples: The parietal pleura lines the inside of the thoracic wall.

entries.meaning: relating to internal organs; the layer of a serous membrane that covers an organ's surface
examples: The visceral pericardium covers the surface of the heart.

entries.meaning: the internal organs, especially those in the ventral cavity
examples: The stomach and intestines are viscera.

entries.meaning: the serous membrane that covers the lungs and lines the thoracic wall
examples: The visceral pleura covers each lung.

entries.meaning: the serous membrane that lines the abdominopelvic wall and covers many of its organs
examples: The visceral peritoneum covers the stomach.

entries.meaning: the thin fluid-filled space between the parietal and visceral peritoneum
examples: Peritonitis can spread through the peritoneal cavity.

entries.meaning: located behind the parietal peritoneum, against the posterior abdominal wall
examples: The kidneys are retroperitoneal organs.

entries.meaning: standing upright, facing forward, feet flat and slightly apart, arms at the sides, palms facing forward with thumbs pointing away from the body
examples: All directional terms assume the body is in anatomical position.

entries.meaning: lying face up, on the back
examples: A patient lies supine for an abdominal exam.

entries.meaning: lying face down, on the abdomen
examples: A patient lies prone for an exam of the back.
